stemMd: Which combination occurs in an ordinary RNA nucleotide?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Glycerol, phosphate and a fatty acid

options.label: C
options.textMd: Ribose, phosphate and a nitrogenous base

explanationMd: An RNA nucleotide combines ribose, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base. DNA differs in its sugar and usual pyrimidine base, while phospholipids and proteins belong to other chemical classes.

distractorRationale.e: Cellulose is a polysaccharide, not a nitrogenous base.
distractorRationale.d: Nucleotides do not contain amino-acid chains.
distractorRationale.a: This is characteristic of a DNA nucleotide.
distractorRationale.b: This describes components associated with phospholipids.
